title: The U.S. dollar issuance constitution — who gave the Fed its role and how it can change
adds: The Fed's role is a statutory operating arrangement created by Congress, not a private agreement or surrender of sovereignty. Issuance is already divided: Congress defines the system; Treasury mints coins and prints notes; the Board orders notes; Reserve Banks place notes and issue reserve balances; banks issue deposit claims. Congress can amend, restrict, move or dissolve by ordinary legislation; an executive order cannot. A retail Fed CBDC is barred through 2030 by FRA §16A.
